title: 3 Events Worth Planning Around Near Seoul This Week (Oct 30 – Nov 7, 2026)
html:
Planning a trip to Korea soon and wondering what's actually happening while you're here, besides the big famous sights? Here are 3 real events taking place in and around Seoul between October 30 and November 7, 2026. None of them need a ticket booked months in advance, and all three are easy to reach by public transportation — perfect if you want your trip to feel a little more "local" than just temple-hopping.

1. Sium Sium Morning — A Free Weekend Walk Along the Han River

"Sium Sium Morning" (쉬엄쉬엄모닝) means something like "a leisurely morning" in Korean, and that's exactly what it is: a free, no-pressure morning event held on weekend mornings, usually 07:00–09:00, somewhere along the Han River (한강, Hangang) — Seoul's big river that cuts the city in half. There's no race, no clock, no entry fee. You can walk, jog, cycle, or just show up with a stroller or your dog. There's also a short fitness-check booth and a few guided stretching/exercise sessions run by instructors, called "GX programs."

This particular series runs through November 29, 2026, rotating between a few different bridges — Gwangjingyo Bridge, Jamsildaegyo Bridge, and Seogang Bridge have all hosted sessions. Because the exact bridge changes week to week, check the event's Instagram (@siumsium.morning) a day or two before you go so you know exactly where to show up. The nearest subway stations to these riverside spots are usually Jamsil Station (Lines 2 & 8) or Gwangnaru Station (Line 5), then a short walk down to the river park.

Good to know for first-timers: "Hangang Park" just means the public park areas that run along both sides of the river — they're free to enter any time, with walking paths, benches, and often food trucks nearby, so even if you miss the exact event time, a walk along the river is a nice, easy activity on its own.

2. 100 Years Night Market — A Retro Night Market in Gangbuk

If you're in Seoul on October 30–31, 2026, this is a fun one for the evening. The "100 Years Market" (백년시장) is a long-running traditional market in Gangbuk-gu, a residential district in northern Seoul that most tourists never visit. A couple of times a year, the market turns into a themed night market called "100 Years Night" — think string lights, a small mirror ball, a mini DJ booth, and food stalls that change up their menu each time. It runs 16:00–21:00 and is free to enter.

A "traditional market" (전통시장, jeontong sijang) in Korea is basically a cluster of small, independent food and goods stalls, usually under a covered street — much more casual and local than a shopping mall, and a great place to try cheap street snacks. The closest subway station is Suyu Station (Line 4), followed by a short bus or taxi ride (around 10 minutes) to the market.

One honest note: night-market dates at small neighborhood markets like this can shift slightly from year to year, so if you want to be extra sure before making a special trip, you can call ahead at +82-2-903-9110 (Gangbuk-gu market office) — or just treat it as a nice bonus stop if you happen to be in the area that weekend.

3. Beautysum Suwon — A K-Beauty Expo Just Outside Seoul

For anyone whose trip is partly a "K-beauty haul" — this one's worth knowing about. Beautysum Suwon (뷰티썸 수원) runs November 5–7, 2026, 10:00–17:00, at the Suwon Convention Center, just south of Seoul. It's a large beauty exhibition covering skincare, makeup, hair, nails, and fragrance brands, with sample booths and brand showcases open to the public, not just industry buyers.

Getting there is easier than it sounds: the venue is about a 10-minute walk from Gwanggyo-jungang Station on the Sinbundang Line, which connects directly to Gangnam in Seoul — no transfers through confusing terminals needed. On entry fees: it's free if you register online in advance (by November 4), or 10,000 won (about $7 USD) if you just show up and register at the door. If you're the type who likes to plan ahead, pre-registering online saves you both money and a line.

Good to know for first-timers: Korean beauty expos like this one are usually a mix of big-name brands and smaller indie brands you won't easily find at home — a good chance to pick up sample sizes before committing to a full-size bottle back home.

💬 Thinking of timing your trip around one of these? Drop a comment below if you have questions — happy to help you plan around it!
meta_description: 3 real events near Seoul this week: a free Han River morning walk, a retro night market in Gangbuk, and a K-beauty expo in Suwon.
